about: This two-panel scene from the animated series Invincible shows Omni-Man flying beside two fighter jets: first glancing over at them, then turning back with a contemptuous scowl and a subtitle sneering at what humans require just to copy "a fraction of our power". He is mocking how much machinery humans need just to fly, something he does effortlessly. As a meme, the jets stand for an elaborate tool, gadget or workaround, and Omni-Man becomes whoever does the same job naturally, smugly unimpressed by the help everyone else needs.
origin: The line comes from season 1, episode 8 of Invincible, the Amazon Prime Video adaptation of the Robert Kirkman comic, which premiered on April 29, 2021, during Omni-Man's brutal fight with his son Mark.
usage:
The subtitle is already in the bottom panel, so you only add two labels. The first box sits in the sky by the jets in the top panel: name the gadget, app or complicated setup. The second box goes in the lower panel near Omni-Man: name the person or thing that achieves the same result with no help.

The classic version pits technology against a skilled human, like a dishwasher against a mom with one sponge, or a GPS against a taxi driver. The bigger the gap between the costly tool and the low-tech champion, the funnier the scowl.
aka: Look What They Need to Mimic a Fraction of Our Power
Mimic a Fraction of Our Power
